title: Lake resorts: Milneburg and West End
summary: He recalls the lakefront resorts, camps with bands, and dancing for forty or fifty cents.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: But you said there were plenty of places in the old days, huh, where you could go to the end of the day.

Well yeah, that's why I mean like the lake, Spanish food, West End, all those places where you could go and that's why most of the people would go. Now, Millenburg was a great big place, you go bathing and it had camps all along. They had a band that played out there, you see, in them different camps. Well, we'd go in from one camp to another, one camp to another, one camp to another. They'd charge me for forty cents or fifty cents to go in and dance. You could rent a bathing suit if you wanted or brought your own bathing suit and go bathing. Well, it's nothing like that. The only place they got now is way out here in the woods, little woods. And it's so obvious getting out there. But a lot of people's out there, though. Christ, woods, people go out there. Well, I never grew up there. You know, I don't like the crowd no more. I don't care for the crowd. No, I don't care for the crowd.
But you liked Millenburg and West End and Spanish food when you were younger?
